title: Cabinet Refinishing Cost in Sugar Land
description: Cabinet refinishing Sugar Land cost: most kitchens run $2,000-$7,000, large ones $10,000+. See what's included, what moves the price, and book a free estimate.
author: Chris Petkau
imageAlt: cabinet refinishing Sugar Land TX — The Proud Paintbrush
content:
Cabinet refinishing in Sugar Land typically runs $2,000–$7,000 for most kitchens, with larger or more complex layouts reaching $10,000 or more. That's the honest answer up front — no teasing, no “call for pricing” runaround — and here's exactly what moves that number up or down.

I'm Chris, owner of The Proud Paintbrush, and I've refinished kitchens all over Sugar Land, from First Colony and Riverstone to Telfair and New Territory. Homeowners here want a real number before they invite anyone in, so here's the straight breakdown of what you're paying for and where a kitchen like yours lands.

What's Included in That Price?

A refinishing quote isn't a bucket of paint and an afternoon. Most of what you pay for is skilled labor and proper prep, because that's what decides whether your cabinets still look factory-smooth in five years. A complete Sugar Land cabinet refinishing job includes:

  • Labor. Removing and labeling every door and drawer front, masking your counters, walls, floors, and appliances, and the careful spray work that follows. This is the bulk of the cost.
  • Prep. Degreasing every surface, sanding and scuffing each face to give the primer a grip, filling dings, and cleaning again. Skipped prep is the number one reason cheap finishes peel at the corners — it's why prep matters more than the paint brand.
  • Materials. A bonding primer made to lock onto slick factory-sealed cabinets, plus a hard-curing, cabinet-grade enamel — not wall paint and not general trim paint.
  • Finish coats. Multiple thin, even coats sprayed to level into a smooth, washable shell, then a cure window so the enamel reaches full hardness.

The paint itself is the cheapest line on the invoice; the rest is craftsmanship. You can see how the pieces break down on our cabinet refinishing pricing page.

What Makes the Price Go Up or Down?

Two kitchens on the same street can quote thousands apart, and it's never random. Here's what moves your number:

  • Cabinet count. More doors, drawers, and linear feet means more to prep and spray. A compact galley sits at the low end; a big open-concept kitchen with an island and a pantry sits at the top.
  • Condition. Sound boxes that just need a color change are straightforward. Grease buildup, water damage, or a failing old finish all add repair and prep labor.
  • Wood vs. MDF. Open-grain woods like the honey-oak in many Fort Bend homes need a grain-managing primer to read smooth; MDF and maple go faster.
  • Paint vs. stain. A sprayed enamel color is the most common and most predictable request. A re-stain or glaze is specialty work, priced differently.
  • Scope. Uppers only, or a single island, costs far less than a full kitchen of boxes, doors, and interiors.

As a rough guide, here's where most Sugar Land kitchens land:

  • Small kitchen: $2,000–$4,000
  • Medium kitchen: $4,000–$7,000
  • Large kitchen: $7,000–$10,000+

Your walkthrough pins down the exact number within those ranges.

How Does Gulf Coast Humidity Affect Cabinet Finishes?

This is a real local factor, not a sales line. Our Gulf Coast humidity means wood moves — it takes on moisture, swells slightly, and dries back out as the seasons and your AC cycle. A finish that can't flex with that movement, or that went over a surface that wasn't fully clean and dry, hairline-cracks at the joints and lifts at the edges. That's why we won't shortcut the degrease, the bonding primer, or the cure time on a Sugar Land kitchen. The right primer-and-enamel system on a properly dried surface is what keeps the finish tight through our muggy summers and cooler, drier winters.

Is Cabinet Refinishing Worth It vs. Replacing?

For most Sugar Land kitchens, it isn't close. New custom cabinets run roughly $10,000–$30,000 and up once you add demolition, countertop removal, and weeks of a torn-up kitchen. Refinishing transforms the exact surfaces you see and touch for a fraction of that — most kitchens fall in the $2,000–$7,000 range — and stays usable through most of the project.

The honest test is simple: if your layout works and the boxes are structurally sound, refinish. If doors are delaminating, boxes are water-damaged, or you're moving the sink or adding an island, replacement is the smarter call. That's the decision we walk through on nearly every estimate with our Sugar Land cabinet refinishing service, and we'll tell you straight which way your kitchen leans.

What Does the Process Look Like with The Proud Paintbrush?

We keep it clean, predictable, and easy to live with:

  • In-home estimate. We walk your kitchen, count cabinets, check condition, talk colors and finish, and hand you a clear written number — no pressure.
  • Prep. Doors and drawers come off and get labeled, your space is fully masked, and every surface is degreased and sanded.
  • Prime. A bonding, stain-blocking primer goes down so the color sits on a surface it can grip.
  • Finish. Cabinet-grade enamel is sprayed in thin, even coats for that furniture-smooth, no-brush-marks result — here's why spraying beats brushing on cabinets.
  • Inspection. We rehang, walk the whole kitchen with you, and don't call it done until you're looking at it and smiling.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does cabinet refinishing take?

Most Sugar Land kitchens take about three to five days on site, depending on the number of doors and drawers. Your kitchen stays usable through most of it, and the enamel keeps curing to full hardness for a week or two after we leave.

Do you paint cabinet boxes and interiors too?

Yes. We refinish the boxes and doors as standard, and we can include the visible interiors and shelves if you want the inside to match. Just tell us at the estimate so it's in the scope and the price.

What finish holds up best in a Sugar Land kitchen?

A hard-curing, cabinet-grade enamel in a satin or semi-gloss sheen. It cures to a washable shell that shrugs off fingerprints, grease, and daily cleaning, and it stands up to our humidity far better than any wall paint.

Can you refinish cabinets that are peeling or already painted?

We can. Previously painted or peeling cabinets just need extra prep — we scrape and sand back the failing finish, spot-prime, and rebuild a sound base before the new coats. It's a common job here, and that prep is exactly why it lasts.

Do I need to empty my cabinets before you start?

Please clear the contents and anything on the counters before day one so we have full access and your dishes stay clean. We handle all the masking, protection, and the rest of the setup ourselves.
